source_text:
nisi si aliud omnino interpretemur idololatrian, quam famulatum idolorum colendorum.,
Male nobis de necessitatibus humanae exhibitionis supplaudimus, si post fidem obsignatam dicimus: non habeo quo uiuam. iam hic enim plenius illi abruptae propositioni respondebo. sero dicitur. ante enim fuit deliberandum ex similitudine prouidentissimi aedificis illius, qui prius sumptus operis cum uiribus suis supputat, ne, ubi coeperit, defectus postea erubescat. sed et nunc habes dicta domini et exempla adimentia tibi omnem causationem. quid enim dicis? egebo. sed felices egenos dominus appellat. uictum non habebo: sed nolite, inquit, cogitare de uictu. et uestitus habemus exemplum lilia. substantia mihi opus erat: atquin omnia uendenda sunt et egentibus diuidenda. sed filiis et posteritati prouidendum: nemo aratro manum imponens et retro spectans aptus est operi. sed condicionalis eram: nemo duobus dominis seruire potest. si uis domini discipulus esse, crucem tuam tollas et dominum sequaris necesse est id est angustias et cruciatus tuos uel corpus solum, quod in modum crucis est. parentes, coniuges, liberi propter deum relinquendi erunt. de artibus et negotiationibus et de professionibus etiam liberorum et parentum causa dubitas? iam tunc demonstratum est nobis et pignera et artificia et negotia propter dominum derelinquenda, cum Iacob et Iohannes uocati a domino et patrem nauemque derelinquunt, cum Matthaeus de teloneo suscitatur, cum etiam sepelire patrem tardum fuit fidei. nemo eorum, quos dominus allegit, non habeo, dixit, quo uiuam. fides famem non timet. scit etiam famem non minus sibi contemnendam propter deum quam omne mortis genus. didicit non respicere uitam, quanto magis uictum? quotusquisque haec adimpleuit? sed quae penes homines difficilia, penes deum facilia. sic tamen nobis de mansuetudine et clementia dei blandiamur, ut non usque ad idololatriae affinitates necessitatibus largiamur, sed omnem afflatum eius uice pestis etiam de longinquo deuitemus, non in his tantum quae praemisimus, sed in uniuersa serie humanae superstitionis, siue deis suis siue defunctis siue regibus mancipatae, ut ad eosdem spiritus immundos pertinentis, modo per sacrificia et sacerdotia, modo per spectacula et hoc genus, modo per festos dies.
thought_title: No excuse of poverty or family can justify contact with idolatry
orientation: Tertullian is answering Christians who, after being baptized, claim they must keep trades connected with idols because they have no other way to live.
pass_a_gloss: unless we interpret idolatry as something else entirely than the service of idols that are to be worshipped. We wrongly congratulate ourselves about the necessities of human livelihood, if after the faith has been sealed we say: I do not have the means to live. For here I will now answer more fully that abrupt proposition. It is said too late. For it should have been deliberated beforehand, after the likeness of that most provident builder, who first reckons the costs of the work together with his own strength, lest, when he has begun, he later blush at his failure. But even now you have the sayings of the Lord and examples that take away from you every excuse. For what do you say? I will be in need. But the Lord calls the poor blessed. I will not have food: but do not, he says, think about food. And for clothing we have the example of the lilies. I needed property: but on the contrary all things are to be sold and divided among the needy. But provision must be made for children and posterity: no one putting his hand to the plow and looking back is fit for the work. But I was a slave by condition: no one can serve two masters. If you wish to be a disciple of the Lord, you must take up your cross and follow the Lord, that is your straits and your torments or the body alone, which is in the manner of a cross. Parents, spouses, children will have to be left behind for God's sake. Do you hesitate about the crafts and trades and about the professions even of children and parents for this reason? Already then it was shown to us that both pledges and crafts and trades are to be left behind for the Lord's sake, when James and John, called by the Lord, leave behind both their father and their boat, when Matthew is roused from the tax booth, when even burying a father was too slow for faith. None of those whom the Lord chose said: I do not have the means to live. Faith does not fear hunger. It knows that hunger is to be despised for God's sake no less than every kind of death. It has learned not to regard life, how much more food? How very few have fulfilled these things? But what is difficult among men is easy with God. Yet let us flatter ourselves about the gentleness and mercy of God in such a way that we do not extend our necessities all the way to the near relations of idolatry, but let us avoid every breath of it, as if it were a plague, even from afar, not only in those things which we have set forth before, but in the whole series of human superstition, whether it has been handed over to their gods or to the dead or to kings, as belonging to the same unclean spirits, now through sacrifices and priesthoods, now through spectacles and things of this kind, now through festal days.

lemmas.gloss: of slave condition, bound by condition

choices.english: the service of idols that are to be worshipped
choices.why: Keeps the gerundive force of colendorum (idols that are to be worshipped) and famulatum as service, matching the glossary sense of idolatry as service of idols.
rejected: the worship of idols to be worshipped

choices.english: after the faith has been sealed
choices.why: Obsignatam means sealed or marked, referring to baptism as the sealing of faith; keeps the metaphor of sealing rather than flattening to 'after baptism.'
Abruptae means broken off or abrupt, referring to the objection 'I have no means to live' as a sudden, cut-off claim; keeps the rhetorical force.

choices.english: I was a slave by condition
choices.why: Condicionalis refers to a person of servile condition or status; rendering as 'slave by condition' preserves the legal-social sense behind the objection.
Affinitas means relationship by marriage or close connection; 'near relations' keeps the sense of close proximity to idolatry without over-translating as 'borders.'

choices.english: every breath of it, as if it were a plague
choices.why: Afflatum is a breath or blast; uice pestis means in the manner of a plague; keeps the vivid image of avoiding even the breath of idolatry like a contagion.
rejected: every influence of it like a disease
every breeze of it as a pestilence

pass_b_english: Unless, of course, we are to interpret idolatry as something other than the service of idols that are to be worshipped.

We flatter ourselves badly about the necessities of human livelihood if, after the faith has been sealed, we say, “I have no means to live.” Here I will answer that abrupt proposition more fully. It is said too late. It should have been deliberated beforehand, like that most provident builder who first reckons the costs of the work against his strength, so that when he has begun he will not later blush at his failure (Luke 14:28-30). But even now you have the Lord’s words and examples to take away every excuse from you. What do you say? “I will be in need.” But the Lord calls the poor blessed (Matthew 5:3). “I will have no food.” But he says, “Do not worry about your life, what you will eat” (Matthew 6:25). And for clothing we have the example of the lilies (Matthew 6:28). “I needed property.” But sell what you have and give to the poor (Matthew 19:21). “But I must provide for children and posterity.” No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the work (Luke 9:62). “But I was making conditions.” No one can serve two masters (Matthew 6:24). If you wish to be the Lord’s disciple, you must take up your cross and follow the Lord (Matthew 16:24)—that is, your hardships and torments, or your body alone, which is shaped like a cross. Parents, spouses, children will have to be left behind for God’s sake (Matthew 19:29). Do you hesitate about arts and trades and professions even for the sake of children and parents? It was shown to us already then that both pledges and crafts and businesses must be abandoned for the Lord’s sake, when James and John, called by the Lord, leave behind both their father and their boat (Matthew 4:21-22), when Matthew is roused from the tax booth (Matthew 9:9), when even burying a father was too slow for faith (Matthew 8:21-22). None of those whom the Lord chose said, “I have no means to live.” Faith does not fear hunger. It knows that hunger must be despised for God’s sake no less than every kind of death. It has learned not to look back at life—how much more at food? How few have fulfilled these things? But what is difficult among men is easy with God (Matthew 19:26).

Still, let us not flatter ourselves about God’s gentleness and mercy to the point of granting our necessities free rein all the way to associations with idolatry. Rather, let us avoid every breath of it, as if it were a plague, even from a distance—not only in the things we have already mentioned, but in the whole series of human superstition, whether it is devoted to their gods, to the dead, or to kings, as belonging to the same unclean spirits, now through sacrifices and priesthoods, now through spectacles and things of that kind, now through festival days.

problems.quote: But I was a slave by condition.
problems.why: 'Condicionalis' here means 'conditional' (i.e., one who makes excuses/conditions), not 'slave by condition.'
problems.ruling: Latin 'condicionalis' = conditional, no 'slave' term; English adds 'slave' changing meaning

all the way to the near relations of idolatry
edits.new: all the way to associations with idolatry

fixed: Changed 'But I was a slave by condition' to 'But I was making conditions' because 'condicionalis' means 'conditional' (one who makes conditions/excuses), not 'slave by condition.'
Changed 'near relations' to 'associations' because 'affinitates' means 'connections/associations/affinities,' not specifically 'near relations' (kinship).

problems.quote: I have no means to live
problems.why: Repeated objection; unclear if new speaker or same.
Matthew 6:25 says 'Do not worry about your life, what you will eat'; 'food' alone narrows.
problems.fix: Quote more fully: 'Do not worry about your life, what you will eat'.

problems.quote: all things are to be sold and divided among the needy
problems.why: Matthew 19:21 says 'sell what you have and give to the poor'; 'divided among the needy' adds element.
Series of imagined objections in quotation marks alternates with Tertullian's responses; some attributions unclear.
problems.fix: Consistently mark each objection and each response with speaker labels or clear punctuation.

fixed: Speaker attribution: the source gives no new speaker marker for the repeated objection; the existing quotation marks already mark it as an objection, so no edit is needed.
Scripture: the source says 'nolite cogitare de uictu' (do not think about food), but the fuller quotation better reflects Matthew 6:25; edited.

Scripture: the source says 'omnia uendenda sunt et egentibus diuidenda' (all things are to be sold and divided among the needy), but Matthew 19:21 says 'sell what you have and give to the poor'; edited.
Speaker attribution: the source alternates objections and responses without explicit markers; the existing quotation marks and paragraph flow already make the alternation clear, so no edit is needed.

last_rejected.quote: How few have fulfilled these things?
last_rejected.why: English adds a claim of fewness; Latin merely asks how many have fulfilled them, not stating the number.
last_rejected.ruling: quotusquisque is a rhetorical idiom meaning 'how few'; not a neutral 'how many' question.

polish.changed: Clarified the objector's voice and the Lord's replies, smoothed sentence rhythm, and kept every claim and Scripture reference intact.

notes.why: Baptismal vow rendered three different ways; reader may miss they are the same vow.
notes.fix: Use 'sacred commitment' consistently; note it means the baptismal vow.
